name: Laelia Pink
lede: Laelia Pink is a moderate, purplish pink named for the orchid genus Laelia, rare in our painting archive and usually hidden there.

sections.title: An orchid's name
sections.body: The library records Laelia Pink from the 1912 Ridgway atlas, plate XXXVIII, hue 67, tone d; the ISCC-NBS system placed it in block 251 in 1955, and Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary carries it too, first recorded 1905, at plate 43 G 2 [1]. The name pairs the orchid genus Laelia with [[pink]]; Laelia itself is not a color name in our library, so it is named here but not linked [1]. In LCH terms it measures lightness 69, chroma 23, hue 359 degrees, the ISCC-NBS "moderate purplish pink" block, Munsell 5.7RP 6.8/5.6, than to plain pink [1]. The nearest named color in the library is [[puce|Puce]], about 5.2 units away by CIEDE2000, a visible difference [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive finds this color in just 18 of 23,781 paintings, 0.08 percent, as photographed; the within-painting lens finds it in 10 [2]. That makes it rarer than 68 percent of the named colors we track [2]. Inside a painting it most often sits as a hidden color, in 40 percent of its appearances, by lightness rank rather than by eye [2].

The earliest match is dated 1531, by Lucas van Leyden; that is 381 years before the name's own first record, in 1912, so the match is a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, not evidence of the actual paint, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2].
